M1.title: Curve and variable offset
M1.notes: No plate-specific calibration. Native dash patterns and offset interpolation differ.

M2.title: Variable-width brush
M2.notes: Calibrated mode changes the width law to match the source's offset-fit envelope. It is not a same-width-law comparison.

M3.title: Latitude spheres
M3.notes: Nominal mode replays MetaPost's scaled random stream for sphere-latitude brush dashes. Calibrated mode uses seed 15 and remains a visual-only comparison.

M4.title: Longitudinal arc tube
M4.notes: Calibrated mode slightly increases maximum hatch width (TeX pt).

M5.title: Suspended sphere composite
M5.notes: Native annotation and arrow construction differ. MetaPost draws the tube before the sphere and uses one global RNG. Use C1 for an isolated sphere measurement.

M6.title: Variable-radius closed tube and taper
M6.notes: Typst reverses the sine sign to account for its opposite circle traversal; this is coordinate conversion. Calibrated mode changes the seed of both tubes.

M7.title: Transverse tube
M7.notes: Calibrated mode changes the dash period (TeX pt). Both modes keep the same drawing resolution.

C1.title: Isolated concentric sphere
C1.notes: No plate-specific calibration. This isolates the sphere from M5's tube and annotations.

S101.title: Stippled brush, sphere and tube
S101.notes: No extra per-plate overrides. The existing Typst density defaults were calibrated previously; they are not upstream parameters. The source uses one global RNG, while Typst uses separate keyed streams.

M8.title: L'Hôpital pulley composites
M8.notes: Uses the source 2.5 mm hatched beam band and 3× minimum rope width. PulleyWheel supplies the thin outer rim; the support is outlined with source thinpen width. The default L'Hôpital figure now omits the non-source l/m labels and uses source-mapped A/B/C offsets; optional length-labels: true retains l/m labels. At 600 ppi whole-plate RMSE is 0.11833 (previous 0.12579), with ink coverage 1.734% vs 2.116%; left/right crop RMSE is 0.13227/0.10421. Wheel/support clipping remains approximate.

M9.title: Wood-grain panels
M9.notes: Same four panel bounds and grain angles. Landscape source blocks swap their internal field axes; the first M9 panel now reproduces the source's first accepted knot coordinate, and accepted knots advance the 28 MetaPost random draws used by their brush rings. Contours use a 1 mm grid, 0.05 pt strokes, per-column offsets and source-sized level jitter. At 600 ppi whole-plate RMSE is 0.22456 with 4.272% ink coverage vs 4.203% source. Contour-brush RNG calls and later-panel stream position remain approximate.

M10.title: Mechanical and optical primitives
M10.notes: The M10 hanging weight uses the source radius 2/5(h−2 mm), 1/4 neck radius, expanding shoulder and body start 2 mm below the attachment, with an approximate source-sized auricle outline. At 600 ppi the full-plate RMSE is 0.07549 (previously 0.07670), and spring/weight crop RMSE is 0.09909 (previously 0.10150). Lens curves, arrowheads and labels still use native algorithms.

M11.title: Globe, eye, knot and refraction
M11.notes: Uses all eight upstream coast polylines. Globe latitude strokes are split into source-style land/ocean masks with the source p1-then-p2 RNG order; the coast brush follows the source projected-radius pen law. Tube-knot hidden intervals expand by 1/sin(crossing angle), approximating projection of the over-strand tube onto the under-strand. Latest 600 ppi trial: whole RMSE 0.12630, globe 0.19552 (prior masked 0.20950; unmasked baseline 0.18935), knot 0.14316 (prior 0.14362). Globe ink coverage is 25.940% → 25.120%; knot coverage is 2.606% → 2.266%; whole-plate ink coverage is 4.917% → 4.774%. Latitude-layer widths, coast RNG phase, curve-time crossing detection and tube-mask edges remain approximate.

S102.title: Tube outline and cast shadow
S102.notes: Same tube path, sphere size, mask polygon and source shadow depth; outline interpolation and shadow projection differ.

S103.title: Solid and glass surface fills
S103.notes: Same source paths, polygons, hatch angles and styles. Defaults follow upstream stroke and row scales, and glass uses the upstream four-row dash cycle. At 600 ppi whole-plate RMSE is 0.21682 (baseline 0.23772); glass RMSE fell to 0.23791 and coverage is 3.87% vs 3.64% source.

S104.title: Flat surfaces
S104.notes: The source +30° hatch maps to -30° on the Typst page because the source fixture flips its vertical axis. At 600 ppi hatch crop RMSE is 0.09247 with ink coverage 13.33% vs 14.07% source; stipple coverage remains close (7.14% vs 7.08%). Whole-plate RMSE is 0.21054 with ink coverage 10.29% vs 10.63%. Hatch stroke shapes and random brush details still differ.

S105.title: Wood block and surface
S105.notes: The plank and wooden surface use the source knot-warped field at a 1 mm grid with source-sized per-contour level offsets, rounded field extents and landscape-axis mapping. Source woodenSurface consumes 536 global random calls through the plank; the first surface knot matches its traced source coordinate within 0.001 mm. At 600 ppi, whole-plate RMSE is 0.10553; block RMSE is 0.13244 and surface RMSE is 0.07909, with surface ink coverage 0.599% vs source 0.489%. Source contour-brush rendering and call counts remain approximate.

S106.title: Standing and hanging weights
S106.notes: The standing weight rises from its base and uses the source radius 2/5h. The hanging weight uses the source radius 2/5(h−2 mm), 1/4 neck radius, expanding shoulder, body start 2 mm below the attachment and an approximate source-sized auricle outline. At 600 ppi full-plate RMSE is 0.07679 (previously 0.07788). Standing crop RMSE is 0.09949 with ink coverage 1.474% vs 1.594% source; hanging crop RMSE is 0.07039 with coverage 1.265% vs 1.131%. The auricle interior, end caps and hatch profiles remain approximate.

S107.title: Wheels and centroid
S107.notes: Both wheels now use upstream radial ring ranges and widths. At 600 ppi pulley-wheel RMSE is 0.09105 with 3.95% coverage vs 3.83% source; wheel RMSE is 0.12807 with 6.03% vs 7.10%. Centroid geometry is shared.

S108.title: Lens and annotation variants
S108.notes: Same convex, concave and plano lens dimensions and annotation geometry; curve and arrow construction differ.
